theory.intro: The mean, the median and the mode are all measures of centre, but they do not all suit every dataset. **Categorical** data — colours, or sizes labelled S, M and L — cannot be added or ordered, so only the **mode** can be used. Numerical data containing an **outlier** distorts the mean, so the **median** is the better figure to report. When the data is numerical and has no outlier, the **mean** is usually best, because it uses the value of every score. Always name the measure you choose and justify the choice in context.
facts: **Mean:** its value depends on every score in the dataset, but it is distorted by outliers and cannot be used with categorical data.
**Median:** it is not distorted by outliers, but it ignores the size of the other scores and may not be a central value.
**Mode:** it is not affected by outliers and is the only measure that works with categorical data, but it may not be a central value.
When the data contains an outlier, report the **median** — the outlier pulls the mean towards itself but barely moves the median.
When the answer has to be a value that really exists, such as a size to order, the **mode** is more useful than a mean such as $11.75$.
A measure of centre is a poor choice when it sits at the very top or the very bottom of the data instead of near the middle.
The range is a measure of spread, not centre, and it is also distorted by outliers.
steps: Check whether the data is categorical
Check the numerical data for an outlier
Name the measure of centre and justify it in context

foundation.question_text:
A shop records the colour of each pair of shoes sold one morning:
black, black, white, brown, black, white, tan, black
Which measure of centre can be used for this data, and what is its value?
foundation.solution_text:
Colours cannot be added or placed in numerical order, so the mean and the median cannot be used.
Only the mode can be used.
Black was sold four times, more often than any other colour, so the mode is black.

foundation.question_text:
A uniform shop sold these T-shirt sizes in one hour:
M, L, M, S, M, XL, L, M, S, L
Which measure of centre should the shop use, and what is its value?
foundation.solution_text:
The sizes S, M, L and XL are categories rather than numbers, so they cannot be added or averaged.
The shop should use the mode.
Size M was sold four times, more often than any other size, so the mode is M.

foundation.question_text:
The yearly salaries of the six staff of a small business are $\$46\,000$, $\$50\,000$, $\$52\,000$, $\$56\,000$, $\$58\,000$ and $\$242\,000$.
$\begin{array}{lc}\textbf{Measure}&\textbf{Value}\\ \hline \text{Mean}&\$84\,000\\ \text{Median}&\$54\,000\end{array}$
Which measure better represents a typical salary? Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
The salary of $\$242\,000$ is an outlier, and it pulls the mean upwards.
The mean of $\$84\,000$ is higher than five of the six salaries, so it is not typical of what the staff earn.
The median of $\$54\,000$ sits among the salaries the staff actually earn, so the median better represents a typical salary.

foundation.question_text: Five houses in a suburb sold last month for $\$720\,000$, $\$740\,000$, $\$760\,000$, $\$780\,000$ and $\$800\,000$. Is the mean an appropriate measure of centre for these prices? Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{3\,800\,000}{5}$
$= \$760\,000$
No price sits far from the others, so there is no outlier to distort the mean.
The mean is appropriate here, and it has the advantage of using the value of every one of the five prices.

foundation.question_text:
A uniform shop sold these sizes of school shorts in one day:
$8$, $10$, $10$, $12$, $12$, $12$, $14$, $16$
The mean size is $11.75$. Explain why the mean is not useful to the shop owner, and state which measure is.
foundation.solution_text:
The shop does not stock a size $11.75$, so the mean is not a size that can be ordered.
$\text{Mode} = 12$
The mode is the most useful measure, because it tells the owner which size sold most often and therefore which size to order more of.

foundation.question_text: The yearly salaries of seven staff, in thousands of dollars, are $30$, $30$, $30$, $30$, $45$, $60$ and $75$. Find the mode and explain why it is a poor measure of centre for this data.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Mode} = 30$
The mode of $\$30\,000$ is the lowest salary in the dataset, and three of the seven staff earn more than it.
A measure of centre should sit near the middle of the data, so the mode is a poor choice here.

foundation.question_text: Five houses in a suburb sold for $\$620\,000$, $\$650\,000$, $\$680\,000$, $\$700\,000$ and $\$1\,875\,000$. An agent advertises that the average price in the suburb is $\$905\,000$. Which measure of centre is the agent using?
foundation.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{4\,525\,000}{5}$
$= \$905\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$680\,000$
The advertised figure matches the mean, so the agent is using the mean.

foundation.question_text: State one advantage and one disadvantage of using the mean as a measure of centre.
foundation.solution_text:
Advantage: the mean depends on the value of every score in the dataset.
Disadvantage: the mean is distorted by outliers, and it cannot be used with categorical data.

development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{4\,000\,000}{5}$
$= \$800\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$660\,000$
The price of $\$1\,400\,000$ is an outlier that pulls the mean above four of the five prices.
The median of $\$660\,000$ best represents a typical price, because it is not distorted by the outlier.

development.question_text:
In a company, seven employees each earn $\$52\,000$ a year and the owner earns $\$430\,000$ a year.
a. Which measure of centre would the owner quote to make the pay look high?
b. Which measure better describes a typical wage?
Justify each answer with a calculation.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{794\,000}{8}$
$= \$99\,250$
$\text{Median} = \$52\,000$
a. The owner would quote the mean of $\$99\,250$, because the one very large salary lifts it well above what any employee is paid.
b. The median of $\$52\,000$ better describes a typical wage, because it is what seven of the eight people actually earn.

development.question_text:
A survey records the colour of every pair of running shoes worn at a fun run:
white, blue, white, black, pink, blue, white, black, white, blue
Explain why neither the mean nor the median can be used here, and state the measure that can.
development.solution_text:
The mean requires the data values to be added together, and colours cannot be added.
The median requires the data to be placed in order, and colours have no meaningful numerical order.
Only the mode can be used. White occurs four times, more often than any other colour, so the mode is white.

development.question_text: Five houses in a suburb sold for $\$780\,000$, $\$795\,000$, $\$810\,000$, $\$825\,000$ and $\$840\,000$. Which measure of centre should be reported? Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
Every price occurs once, so this data has no mode.
$\overline{x} = \frac{4\,050\,000}{5}$
$= \$810\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$810\,000$
No price sits far from the others, so there is no outlier to distort the mean.
The mean of $\$810\,000$ should be reported, because it uses every price and here it agrees with the median.

development.question_text: Five houses in a small street sold for $\$520\,000$, $\$560\,000$, $\$900\,000$, $\$900\,000$ and $\$900\,000$. Find the median and explain why it is not a central value for this data.
development.solution_text:
$520\,000, 560\,000, 900\,000, 900\,000, 900\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$900\,000$
The median is equal to the highest price in the street, so it sits at the top of the data rather than near its middle.
A median can fail in this way because it counts positions only and ignores how far apart the values are.

development.question_text: The yearly salaries of eight staff, in thousands of dollars, are $40$, $42$, $44$, $46$, $46$, $48$, $50$ and $176$. A union says a typical salary is $\$46\,000$, while management says it is $\$61\,500$. State which measure of centre each side is using, and which is more appropriate here.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{492}{8}$
$= 61.5$
$\text{Median} = \frac{46 + 46}{2}$
$= 46$
Management is using the mean of $\$61\,500$ and the union is using the median of $\$46\,000$.
The salary of $\$176\,000$ is an outlier that lifts the mean above seven of the eight salaries, so the union's median is the more appropriate measure.

development.question_text: Five blocks of land in a suburb sold for $\$480\,000$, $\$495\,000$, $\$510\,000$, $\$530\,000$ and $\$1\,650\,000$. An agent wants to advertise the suburb as expensive, while a buyer wants to know what a typical block costs. State the measure of centre each of them would prefer, with a reason.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{3\,665\,000}{5}$
$= \$733\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$510\,000$
The agent would quote the mean of $\$733\,000$, because the outlier of $\$1\,650\,000$ lifts it above four of the five prices.
The buyer would prefer the median of $\$510\,000$, because it is not distorted by the outlier and is close to what most blocks cost.

mastery.question_text: A clothing store records two things about every customer at a sale: the size of the T-shirt bought, which is S, M, L or XL, and the amount spent. The amounts spent, in dollars, were $28$, $32$, $35$, $38$, $40$, $42$ and $310$. State which measure of centre the store should use for each set of data, and justify each choice.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Check whether the data is categorical**
The T-shirt sizes are categories, so they cannot be added or placed in numerical order.
Only the mode can be used for the sizes, and it also tells the store which size to stock most of.
2. **Check the numerical data for an outlier**
$\overline{x} = \frac{525}{7}$
$= \$75$
$\text{Median} = \$38$
The amount of $\$310$ is an outlier that lifts the mean above six of the seven amounts.
3. **Name the measure of centre and justify it in context**
Use the mode for the sizes and the median of $\$38$ for the amounts spent.

mastery.question_text: A start-up advertises that its mean starting salary is $\$96\,000$. In fact seven of its workers each earn $\$34\,000$ and the founder earns $\$530\,000$. Explain why the advertised figure is misleading, and state the measure of centre that should be reported instead.
mastery.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{768\,000}{8}$
$= \$96\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$34\,000$
The founder's salary of $\$530\,000$ is an outlier that pulls the mean far above every worker's pay, so nobody who starts at the company earns anything close to $\$96\,000$.
The median of $\$34\,000$ should be reported instead, because it is what seven of the eight people actually earn.

mastery.question_text: Eight houses in a suburb sold for, in thousands of dollars, $600$, $600$, $600$, $600$, $900$, $1000$, $1100$ and $2000$. Find the mean, median and mode, then explain what is wrong with reporting the mode as the typical price and what is wrong with reporting the mean.
mastery.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{7\,400}{8}$
$= 925$
$\text{Median} = \frac{600 + 900}{2}$
$= 750$
$\text{Mode} = 600$
The mode of $\$600\,000$ is the lowest price in the dataset, so it is not a central value.
The mean of $\$925\,000$ is higher than five of the eight prices, because it is pulled up by the most expensive house.
The median of $\$750\,000$ is the measure that best represents a typical price here.
